facts.text: Portola Valley named after Spanish explorer Gaspar de Portolá, who led first European party to San Francisco Peninsula in 1769.
The town sits on eastern slopes of Santa Cruz Mountains, nestled on San Francisco Peninsula.
Our Lady of the Wayside Church, built 1912, is a California Historic Landmark serving local Catholic community.
The area’s written history dates to 1833 when Governor Figueroa granted a square league to Domingo Peralta and Máximo Martínez, forming Rancho Cañada del Corte de Madera.
Hallidie, a wire rope manufacturer, built his home Eagle Home Farm in Portola Valley and in 1894 erected a 7,341‑foot tramway to Skyline’s peak, removed after his death.
In 1964 Portola Valley incorporated and adopted single‑family zoning, setting a 1‑acre minimum lot that later grew to 3.5 acres, shaping its affluent, low‑density character.
